title: Growing up in Napoleonville and learning trombone
summary: Nelson was raised in Napoleonville, studied trombone with Professor Williams and admired Lawrence Johnson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And did you spend your early childhood in New Orleans?
No, I left New Orleans when I was about two months old. Went to a place out in the country named Napoleonville. I spent about 25 years out there.
Did they have any bands out there in the Polandville? Yes.

They had Clayman Williams and they had Joseph Garber. Clayman Williams, Professor Williams, he taught me the trombone. My mother, she wanted me to play piano. But I'd rather play the trombone. I liked the trombone better than I did the piano.
Mm-hmm. Did they have any trombones out there you were in the...
Yes, they had a fellow by the name of Lawrence Johnson. He was playing with a band out there. And they left to go to Lake Charles, Louisiana. And I said I always wanted to play a trombone like him.
Do you play like him today?
No, pretty close. He played smooth and he could play rough and he could play jazz. Mm-hmm. Try to get off and things like that, yes.
